description: When the idle is produced by the EOT prediction of an earlier burst rather than by the last burst, rule 1 does not apply even though the last burst met two-node condition (a): the VDCD-determined idle gets lbt_wait_vdcd_ms.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047); its S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is data queued for transmission and produces no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096). Every received D_PDU is a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA (type 7, address size 4, C_PDU ID as stated, reception window 20) whose segment is a DATA C_PDU holding a DATA S_PDU from SAP 9 to SAP 9 with U_PDU "hi". At 2000: a D_PDU from 0.0.1.3 to 0.0.1.9 (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 16, end 10000); the burst is lost at 3000, so csma.vdcd_end runs 7000 ms. At 3500 a burst from 0.0.1.9 starts (csma.vdcd_end cancelled, DCD busy); at 4000 a D_PDU from 0.0.1.9 to this node, individual (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 10, end 9000), whose S_PDU is for SAP 9, which no client has bound, so delivering it (P3-6) gives no output (A-0235). That burst meets condition (a), but its end at 4500 and its own end time 9000 come before the carried end time 10000 (C-1024), so the idle at 10000 is produced by the first transmission, which does not meet it (K-0072). At 4500 csma.vdcd_end 5500 ms; at 10000 rule 3 gives 3000 ms. Since corpus 0.7.0 the DTS also keeps dts.ttd at the earliest TTD in its transmit queue: started when a request becomes the earliest, cancelled when the transmit queue empties (C-1050).
